chunks: Say: "O men, if you have doubt about my faith, then (know) I do not worship those you worship apart from God, but I worship God who makes you die; and I am commanded to be a believer,
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet (SAW) say about his worship in relation to those who doubt his faith?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Yunus, this verse serves as a definitive declaration of Tawhid (monotheism) and the Prophet's distinct identity, contrasting his exclusive worship of Allah with the polytheistic practices of the Qurayh. Shia scholarship often highlights this as a model for clear theological stance-taking, emphasizing that true faith requires both internal conviction and external consistency in worship. The phrase 'I have been commanded' underscores the prophetic obedience to divine instruction, reinforcing the concept of Imamate and guidance as a divinely mandated path.
